title: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks
mechanism: Confident-learning style detection of test-set label errors; errors can flip model rankings.
adaptation: Flag val/test cells whose crack or inactive labels disagree strongly with the 5-fold OOF ensemble (CSIR_00070_r8_c4 is a known case); report rankings with and without flagged cells; no manual relabelling.
min_experiment: Arm: remove top flagged cells. Baseline: clean-49. Metric: rank change of house vs PF vs ensemble. Kill: no rank flip and |delta change| < 0.005.
evidence: R: label errors found in test sets of 10 common CV/NLP/audio datasets; rankings change on corrected subsets.
prior_overlap: partial: one noisy cell already excluded by hand; audit flagged 24 of 239 train cells, nothing systematic on test/val.

alt_notes.adaptation: After models are frozen, run label-error ranking on the 50 test and 106 E1 cells (labels only), count crack/inactive errors, report every method on original and audited labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: audit test/E1 labels with ensemble ranking + cleanlab; re-rank the 5-seed house, PF and ensemble models. Kill: none (benchmark instrument).

alt_notes.adaptation: Rank test and E1 cells by disagreement between the OOF ensemble and the label at crack-component level. Review only the top few flags (minimal, allowed under the no-labelling rule). Publish rankings on both label sets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: OOF disagreement ranking, then rankings of house vs PF vs ensemble on original vs corrected test labels. Decision: if any pair flips, publish both leaderboards.
